MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Whyalla - Medical Scientist





Job no: 943897

Work type: Full time

Located in: Eyre and Western

Categories: Science, Engineering, Technical




 
Central Adelaide Local Health Network

Statewide - SA Pathology

MeS1 $71,046 to $86,729 p.a. (pro-rata) + Superannuation & Salary Sacrifice Benefits

SA, Whyalla 5600

Full Time, Permanent Role

About the role

Join SA Pathology as a Medical Scientist in Whyalla and become part of a supportive regional laboratory delivering high-quality diagnostic services to the local community. You'll apply your scientific expertise across multiple pathology disciplines, perform routine diagnostic testing and contribute to timely, accurate results that support exceptional patient care.

Working closely with experienced colleagues, clinicians and healthcare providers, you'll gain broad hands-on experience while contributing to service improvement and the introduction of new techniques. Whyalla sits at the top of the Eyre Peninsula, where the outback meets the sea. From Hummock Hill Lookout and the picturesque foreshore to the world-famous Giant Australian Cuttlefish migration, the region offers an outstanding lifestyle with easy access to the Eyre Peninsula, a welcoming community, sporting clubs, and convenient Qantas flights connecting you to Adelaide and beyond.

About You

You are a motivated Medical Scientist who enjoys working in a collaborative laboratory environment and delivering quality diagnostic services.

- Relevant Medical Science degree recognised by NPAAC

- Perform quality diagnostic testing with accuracy

- Work collaboratively across multidisciplinary teams

- Maintain laboratory equipment and solve technical issues

- Prioritise workloads and deliver excellent service

About us

Statewide Clinical Support Services (SCSS) is a unique public healthcare organisation that serves health consumers and provides specialist clinical services to the health system in South Australia. SCSS encompasses BreastScreen SA, SA Dental, SA Medical Imaging, SA Pathology, and SA Pharmacy. Come and work with us to improve the health and well-being of South Australians, across all age groups and at any time of their life or health need. 

What we offer

Salary Benefits: Enjoy flexible salary packaging options, including up to $9,010 each FBT year for living expenses (such as mortgage, rent, utilities and groceries) plus an additional $2,650 for meal and entertainment expenses.

Professional Development: Opportunity to apply for reimbursement of eligible professional development activities, and access to dedicated leave for ongoing learning.

Annual Leave: Enjoy paid recreation leave for essential rejuvenation, with leave loading applied.

Health and Fitness Benefits: Access to Fitness Passport, a discounted workplace health and fitness program for you and your family, plus an annual voluntary flu vaccination to support your wellbeing.

Employee Assistance Program: Confidential counselling and support services for you and your family via our Employee Assistance Program.

Regional Incentive Payment: Rewarding your impact in regional communities with an annual payment of up to $882 for eligible MMM3 locations, in accordance with the Allied Health Professionals, Assistants and Psychologists Enterprise Agreement 2025.

Diversity and inclusion:

Statewide supports and fosters a culture in which employees feel they belong and feel safe at work. The culture aims to encourage all people to use their talents and to be valued and rewarded for their contributions.

Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander applicants are encouraged to apply. 

Application Information:

Please refer to the role description for essential educational-vocational qualifications that may be required.

Appointment will be subject to a satisfactory Criminal History Check and compliant Immunisation screening as indicated in the role description.

SA Health Services are required to implement the Addressing vaccine preventable disease: Occupational assessment, screening and vaccination policy in the workplace.

Please note that unsolicited applications from recruitment agencies or third parties will not be accepted for this position.

Work type: Full time

Located in: Adelaide CBD

Categories: Allied and Scientific Health




 

Central Adelaide Local Health Network (CALHN)

The Royal Adelaide Hospital 

Salary ASO-3 $74,095 - $78,694 p.a. + super + salary packaging

Full-time temporary up to 12 months (with the possibility of becoming permanent)

About CALHN
At Central Adelaide (CALHN), we're shaping the future of health through excellence in clinical care, research, and innovation. As South Australia's largest health network, we deliver exceptional, safe and connected healthcare - for our patients, our community, and our people.

With more than 17,000 dedicated employees, every day at CALHN presents an opportunity to make a real impact-not because it's expected, but because our values guide us to be our best. Find out more about CALHN sites and services, our stories and the opportunities to be part of CALHN.

About the Role

The role is to Coordinate and undertake the collection, validation, entry, submission and reporting of cardiothoracic surgical data for the Royal Adelaide Hospital to national clinical registries including ANZSCTS and ANZTHOR. The role contributes to clinical governance, quality improvement, benchmarking, research and service planning by ensuring the provision of accurate, timely and complete data in accordance with legislative, ethical and organisational requirements.Ideally, an ANZSCTS Data Manager would possess the following skills and experience:

Cardiac nursing or ICU nursing experience (or equivalent)

Competency with Microsoft Office software (Word, Excel)

Proficiency in the use of web browsers

Strong communication and interpersonal skills

Excellent organisation and time management skills

Proven experience with data entry and attention to detail

About You

You're an organised and detail focused professional who enjoys turning clinical data into meaningful insights while supporting quality patient care.

- Experience in clinical data or health registries
- Skilled in data analysis with strong attention to detail
- Manage priorities and work with initiative
- Build strong relationships across healthcare teams
- Understand data privacy, governance and quality standards

Why You'll Love It Here - CALHN benefits that matter
We know that a great career is about more than just the work you do, it's also about the support you receive. At CALHN, you'll enjoy :

Salary packaging - up to $9,010 for living expenses + $2,650 for meals & entertainment + pre-tax super & novated lease options

Safe connections - be part of a culture of safety and connectivity, focusing on outcomes and continuous improvements

Recognition & growth - celebrate success and explore opportunities across CALHN's many sites

Flexible work options - speak to us about flexibility options for this role to suit your lifestyle

Paid leave - with leave loading for rest and recharge

Health & fitness perks - discounted access to Fitness Passport & free flu vaccinations

Wellbeing support - Employee Assistance Program for you & your family

Diversity & Inclusion
We're committed to building an inclusive workplace where everyone feels safe, respected, and supported. We strongly encourage applications from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, people with disabilities, culturally diverse backgrounds, and LGBTQIA+ communities.

Application Information

Please refer to the role description for essential educational-vocational qualifications that may be required 945496 RD Data Manager CTSU.pdf

Appointment will be subject to satisfactory Criminal History Clearances and compliant immunisation screening as indicated in the role description.

For nearly 25 years, APD Global has set the benchmark in delivering advanced, comprehensive, and specialised engineering solutions.

We have around 800 employees including our alliance contracting partners, across 15 strategically located offices in Australia (Perth, Sydney, Melbourne, Brisbane, Adelaide, Darwin), New Zealand and Malaysia. We specialise in seamless integration across the Power Systems, Telecommunications, and Renewable Energy industries. Our expertise spans Power Systems Studies, Transmission Lines, Substations, Telecommunications, Protection, Control & Automation, Renewable Energy Connections, Mining, and Engineering, Protection Panel Design and Installation, 3D Design and Manufacturing as well as Construction/Management (EPC/M) services.

We have outstanding opportunity for a highly experienced and skilled ENGINEERING TECHNOLOGIST to join our team across all states in Australia. We are looking for trustworthy individuals with integrity who will bring a positive can-do attitude to the position and to the team. Position available in Vic, Qld, WA, 
and NSW.

The Role
A space-based Engineering Technologist at a power company primarily uses satellite technology to enhance the power grid. This role requires the successful candidate to manage projects from start to finish, ensuring the effective and cohesive operation of both space and ground systems to meet the company's operational and strategic goals.

Key duties involve: Designing and implementing satellite communication systems, Utilising satellite data for grid analysis, and Integrating space-based technology into existing ground infrastructure.

Core duties
System design and architecture: Design and define the architecture for satellite-based communication, monitoring, or sensing systems to be used by the power company. This includes analyzing performance and technical specifications.
Power and communication integration: Ensure that satellite power systems and communication links are compatible with the power company's ground infrastructure and can transmit data and commands reliably.
Mission and project management: Oversee the entire lifecycle of a project, including research, design, development, testing, and deployment of space-based assets, ensuring they meet the company's objectives.
Stakeholder management: Coordinate with internal teams (e.g., grid operations, IT, finance) and external partners (e.g., satellite operators, vendors) to ensure seamless integration and collaboration.
Data analysis: Work with and analyze data from satellites to support power grid management, such as monitoring assets, predicting demand, or assessing grid health and stability.
Technical oversight: Ensure that all subsystems of a space-based system function correctly together, addressing any integration issues or performance bottlenecks that arise.
Testing and validation: Develop and execute test plans for new systems and validate that they meet performance and safety requirements before and during deployment.
Risk and compliance management: Identify and manage risks associated with using space-based technology and ensure compliance with relevant regulations and standards.

Example scenario:
A power company might employ a space-based systems engineer to create a system for real-time monitoring of remote substations. The engineer would design a system using a constellation of small satellites to collect data.

Their duties would include:
Defining the requirements for the satellite communication system, including data rates and latency.
Designing the satellite payload and its integration with the company's ground control software.
Ensuring the system's power budget is adequate for its mission lifespan.
Testing the system on the ground to verify its performance before launch.
Collaborating with the satellite operator to ensure smooth data delivery once the system is operational

If you have the skills required for this role and you feel this is the job for you, then apply now!
Salary: Between $79,499 and $82,000 per annum + Super

MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Monash Health exists to reimagine care, so that people can live their best lives. 






We provide safe and equitable care, for every stage of life, delivered with world-leading expertise and over 175 years of experience. 






As a leading academic health service, we're committed to providing tomorrow's care today by integrating research, teaching and training into everyday practice. 






Our team of 24,000 people are full hearted, open minded and all in. Together, we provide more than 250 integrated services for every stage of life at over 50 locations and in the community across south-east Melbourne, Victoria, serving 1.2 million residents in the South Metro Local Health Service Network. 


Are you currently part of the team at Monash Health? Use your network login to access the Monash Health Careers portal and discover all the job opportunities open to you, to support growing your career within the organisation.




To see first-hand what our colleagues think about working here, take a look at the following short videos monashhealth.org-careers.







Supportive on the job development to grow your career 












Various additional leave options 












Based at Monash Medical Centre in Clayton 















Help shape the future of healthcare at Monash Health and embark on a rewarding career where your dedication makes a difference in people's lives. 






This role involves performing routine diagnostic laboratory tests according to established protocols to support patient care within Monash Health Pathology services. The position works under the supervision of a Principal Scientist and contributes to accurate, timely pathology results. Key aspects include: 









Laboratory testing: Performing haematology analyses in line with established protocols 












Morphology expertise: Demonstrated experience in blood film morphology, including identification and reporting of abnormalities 












Quality & safety: Adhering to quality assurance, control procedures, and safety standards 












Equipment & processes: Maintaining instruments, handling specimens and escalating abnormal or unexpected results 












Teamwork & communication: Working collaboratively with laboratory teams and contributing to efficient service delivery 












Flexibility: Availability for casual rotating roster across haematology services 















About the Department - Program






Alfred Health and Monash Health have established a formal partnership to deliver a Shared Pathology Service as one of two pathology networks for metropolitan Melbourne. All roles in the Pathology Programs are working to develop the Partnership and ensure we continue to provide high quality care for the patients across the health services. 






Monash Health Pathology is an integral part of Monash Health. It is the largest public provider of Pathology services in the state and currently operates 6 laboratories. The largest of these is located at the Monash Medical Centre, Clayton, with additional laboratories located at the Dandenong, Moorabbin, Casey, Victorian Heart Hospital and Wonthaggi Hospitals. There are currently 18 collection locations based within the hospital sites and community settings. Services are provided to the Public and Private sectors, and other laboratory services. 












About the Role 






Join the Monash Health Pathology team as a Medical Scientist Grade 1 within Haematology. In this role, you will work under the guidance of the Principal Scientist and collaborate closely with the broader multidisciplinary laboratory team across the Central Laboratory. 









The role focuses on delivering high-quality diagnostic services including routine haematology testing, transfusion testing and blood product support, and blood film morphology assessment, ensuring accurate and timely results to support patient care. You will perform laboratory testing in accordance with established protocols, carry out quality control procedures, and maintain laboratory equipment and processes. 












The Medical Scientist is responsible for ensuring the quality and safety of results at the point of care, recognising and escalating abnormal findings and contributing to continuous quality improvement initiatives. 












This role requires the ability to work both independently and collaboratively, with strong analytical skills, attention to detail and effective communication. A commitment to professional development, flexibility to work rostered and after hours shifts, and the ability to manage a varied workload in a fast-paced environment are essential. 












Experience in blood film morphology is highly valued, supporting accurate interpretation and reporting within haematology services. 












The role is a 24-7 rotational position with shifts that include day, early, afternoon, evening, overnight and weekend shifts. Particiaption in the on call roster.















About You 






To be successful in this healthcare role, you will bring the following demonstrated skills, experience, and attributes: 









Bachelor of Biomedical Science (Medical Laboratory Science) or recognised equivalent is essential 












Demonstrated experience or strong interest in haematology laboratory testing, including routine analysis and workflows 












Demonstrated experience or strong interest in transfusion science, including testing and blood product support. 












Proven experience in blood film morphology and the ability to accurately identify and interpret abnormal findings (highly regarded) 












Sound knowledge of laboratory instrumentation, quality control, and quality assurance procedures 












Strong analytical, problem-solving, and organisational skills with high attention to detail 












Ability to work both independently and collaboratively within a multidisciplinary team 












Excellent verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to effectively liaise with staff at all levels 












Demonstrated ability to work efficiently under pressure and meet clinical turnaround times 












Commitment to maintaining professional standards, ongoing learning, and participating in quality improvement initiatives 















Why you will love working with us 






Ours is a connected team with strong shared values and an unwavering commitment to excellence. We are a highly skilled, collaborative, and welcoming team where the only limit in your career is you. Upon your appointment, we will provide you with:









A supportive and cohesive sub-team, working within a larger consumer relations team. 












Professional develop
